newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks drift lower in dull trade by noon.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks drift lower in dull trade by noon.

text.p: AORD 2711.70 -21.7 DJIA July 4 Holiday
SPI Sycom 2744.0 -21.0 US 30yr July 4 Holiday
10yrbond futs 93.185 -0.005 Gold NY closed Lon fix 324.45
AUD $0.7474 (Fri cl $0.7521) CRB Index July 4 Holiday
*Stocks broadly down in light trade, investors deserting gold shares after RBA gold sale. Volume 145.03 million, value A$233.26 million, 1,013 stocks traded, 325 steady, 148 up, 540 down.
Australian shares drifted steadily lower in dull trade on Monday as investors waited for new direction from the U.S. after the Independence Day long weekend.
"Trading has been very light ever since this morning. Our market has just drifted off today and now we're waiting to see what happens overseas tonight," one dealer said.
At 12.25 p.m. (0225 GMT), the All Ordinaries index had shed 21.7 points to 2,711.7 in low turnover worth A$233 million.
September share price index futures contracts were 21 points lower at 2,744, a 32.3 point premium to the underlying market.
Gold stocks remained hurt by the Reserve Bank's gold sale.
The sector index slumped another 5.1 percent after last week's news that the RBA had sold two thirds of its gold reserves, pulling down gold prices on the world market.
"I think gold stocks will probably stay around these levels unless gold prices fall more," one senior dealer said.
Newcrest Mining lost 16 cents to A$3.04 and Lihir Gold 16 to A$1.87. Sons of Gwalia, which defied losses on Friday, dipped 20 cents to A$4.70 in low turnover.
Normandy Mining lost six cents to A$1.35 in fairly active trade despite optimistic comments from the company.
Normandy Mining's executive chairman Robert Champion de Crespigny said in a statement he expected further profit growth in 1997/98 despite lower gold prices.
Among the relatively actively traded blue chips, Broken Hill Pty Co ltd lost 35 cents to A$19.25, while WMC lost 14 cents to A$8.13.
"The two of them are pulling the market down," one dealer said, adding some investors were taking home profits in BHP after the recent run.
Rio Tinto fell back from early gains and traded eight cents lower at A$22.35.
